name: Thoreum V4 self-transfer balance doubling
summary: The V4 implementation's transfer accounting credited the recipient without debiting the sender when both are the same address, so any account could call transfer(self, balanceOf(self)) and have its recorded THOREUM balance grow by the post-fee transfer amount. The campaign repeatedly doubled small acquired balances and sold the unsupported tokens into the THOREUM/WBNB BiSwap pair. The defect is permissionless executable logic in the implementation the project itself authored, deployed and installed; the privileged upgrade is the code-change event, not the cause.

loss.notes: The coherent campaign is 36 successful calls from the same EOA to the same helper, from block 24912667 through block 24913336. Receipt Transfer-log netting gives the THOREUM/WBNB BiSwap pair 0xd822e1737b1180f72368b2a9eb2de22805b67e34 an exact aggregate delta of -3194.414045570313325194 WBNB after already subtracting 1.7735 WBNB of identifiable campaign inputs. Of the gross WBNB outputs, 2261.490132565026795779 WBNB went to attacker beneficiary 0x1285fe345523f00ab1a66acd18d9e23d18d2e35c and 934.697413005286529415 WBNB went through the BiSwap router as the token's transfer-fee machinery. The legacy ~2,000/2,260 BNB reports measure attacker proceeds rather than the pair's exact pre-recovery depletion. No recovery was identified.

lastCodeChange.description: upgradeTo(address) selected 0x79fe086a4c03c5e38ff8074dea9ee0a18dc1af4f in Upgraded log 0. The EIP-1967 implementation slot contains 0x0743931af9ce6a0dbd8d8d664c3d87d0bb797d2c at block 24910633 and 0x79fe086a4c03c5e38ff8074dea9ee0a18dc1af4f from block 24910634 through the pre-anchor block 24912666. Runtime hash 0x79f89e49910917df2c2f6e904235ca553b292e6de6b97311e01079b41e56252f is identical at implementation deployment block 24910631 and pre-anchor block 24912666.

sources.note: The v1 anchor was transaction 0x3fe3a1883f0ae263a260f7d3e9b462468f4f83c2c88bb89d1dee5d7d24262b51, nonce 33, which yielded only 6.109951473560231892 WBNB to the beneficiary. Scanning the sender's onchain history and the pair's WBNB flows identifies 36 successful same-selector calls to helper 0x7d1e1901226e0ba389bfb1281ede859e6e48cc3d, nonces 5-41 except the unrelated nonce-11 native transfer. Transaction 0x5058c820fa0bb0daff2bd1b30151cf84c618dffe123546223b7089c8c2e18331 is the earliest successful defect execution at block 24912667, index 20; the final call is 0x885262f9bcccf8f80bb1a2173a5e3dd2f9c27a0dead0215139b983a7702ead34 at block 24913336. Exact receipt netting produces the recorded pair depletion. Proxy deployment, implementation deployment, Upgraded log 0, EIP-1967 slot transition, and stable runtime hashes establish the artifact and 6,134-second activation age. Cohort classification remains provisional: the privileged project address 0x6a963573b9a7aaef9cb9eee747e1b6b2c21b0520 deployed V4 implementation 0x79fe086a4c03c5e38ff8074dea9ee0a18dc1af4f at block 24910631 and activated it three blocks later; Hypernative's published timeline attributes this to a compromised key, while CertiK reports the team's statement that the vulnerability arose in its newly updated V4. If the privileged key was compromised and V4 was malicious attacker-installed machinery, the incident is excluded by METHODOLOGY.md rather than admitted as a code-age observation.

Cohort decision on the compromised-key question, settled on onchain evidence. (1) Authorship and installation: the same EOA 0x6a963573b9a7aaef9cb9eee747e1b6b2c21b0520 created the ERC1967 proxy 0xce1b3e5087e8215876af976032382dd338cf8401 on 2022-07-15 (block 19566917), created V4 implementation 0x79fe086a4c03c5e38ff8074dea9ee0a18dc1af4f at block 24910631 with nonce 6172, and installed it three blocks later with nonce 6173 via a bare upgradeTo(address) call (input 0x3659cfe600000000000000000000000079fe086a4c03c5e38ff8074dea9ee0a18dc1af4f, 20 gwei, 36371 gas, one Upgraded log). (2) Routine, not a takeover: this was the ninth Upgraded event on the proxy and the fifth in two days (blocks 24886594, 24890329, 24897307, 24900551, 24910634), each preceded by the same key creating the implementation one to three blocks earlier; the immediately preceding implementation 0x0743931af9ce6a0dbd8d8d664c3d87d0bb797d2c was created at nonce 6168 and installed at nonce 6169 in the same pattern ten hours before. (3) No interruption of control: the sender's nonce sequence is strictly continuous across the whole window (6106 through 6361 in blocks 24880969-24944662) and interleaves ordinary token administration on the proxy with the V4 deployment, so there is no gap, no key rotation, no ownership or admin transfer, and no privileged withdrawal anywhere in the series. (4) The drain came from an outsider: EOA 0x1ae2dc57399b2f4597366c5bf4fe39859c006f99 first appears at block 24912357 with nonce 0, funded with 3.129123 and 1.982309 BNB from 0x4727250679294802377dd6ca6541b8e459077c95, deploys helper 0x7d1e1901226e0ba389bfb1281ede859e6e48cc3d at block 24912457 and starts the campaign at block 24912667, 1h42m after V4 went live; it has no funding or nonce relationship to the project key. (5) The project kept operating the contract afterwards: at nonces 6194-6197 it deployed and installed replacements 0xc04eaf617c070934c7e1aec895682f98f1987fc9 and 0xeb1d237ed06d3dcd6c8867e939bbc68780ef91a7, at nonce 6201 it re-installed 0x79fe086a4c03c5e38ff8074dea9ee0a18dc1af4f itself, at nonces 6198-6242 it spent its own BNB buying THOREUM through the BiSwap and PancakeSwap routers, and it continued upgrading the same proxy from the same key for nearly two more years, the last observed Upgraded event being block 44192300 on 2024-11-21 sent with nonce 8227. A compromised key would have left the project unable to upgrade, and no attacker returns an upgrade key or re-installs the code the victim replaced. The compromise story is therefore not supported onchain; the incident is a project-authored code defect and is admitted. (6) Defect reproduced: in the anchor trace the helper holds 452.650578005831142846 THOREUM, calls transfer(0x7d1e1901..., 452650578005831142846) on the proxy, the delegatecall into 0x79fe086a emits a 67.897586700874671426 fee Transfer to the token and a 384.752991304956471420 Transfer from the helper to itself, and balanceOf then returns 769.505982609912942840 = 452.650578005831142846 + 384.752991304956471420. No parameter value makes that accounting correct, so the METHODOLOGY boundary test admits it as a code-age observation. (7) Loss re-reproduced independently: netting WBNB Transfer logs over the 36 receipts in source-2 gives pair 0xd822e1737b1180f72368b2a9eb2de22805b67e34 an inflow of 234.173569816004373934 WBNB, an outflow of 3428.587615386317793309 WBNB and an exact net of -3194414045570313325194 wei; at the DefiLlama BNB price 290.66518685527615 for 1674104507 that is 928504.9554488137 USD. The campaign runs from block 24912667 index 20 to block 24913336 index 80. (8) Anchors re-checked: runtime hash of 0x79fe086a is 0x79f89e49910917df2c2f6e904235ca553b292e6de6b97311e01079b41e56252f, the verifier reproduces the 6134-second age, the deployment at 19566917:9, the last code change at 24910634:0 and the Upgraded topic1 selection.
